item.text: I’ll inspect the CSV reader and tests first to see the existing parser shape and the exact failure modes, then patch the implementation and run the unittest suite.
The repo is very small and the worktree is clean. I’m reading the implementation and tests now, then I’ll add focused cases if the existing tests don’t cover every requested behavior.

The current implementation splits physical lines and commas directly, so the safest fix is to delegate CSV tokenization to Python’s `csv.reader` while preserving the existing `parse_records(text)` API and blank-line skipping behavior. I’m adding regression tests for the requested cases before patching.
Regression coverage is in place. Next I’m replacing the parser internals with the standard CSV parser and keeping the blank-line filter explicit so whitespace-only records stay ignored.
The implementation is patched. I’m running the benchmark’s unittest command now, and I’ll also check the diff afterward for anything unintended.

diff --git a/src/csv_records.py b/src/csv_records.py
index 36c4b79..09576f9 100644

@@ -1,7 +1,6 @@
+import csv
+from io import StringIO
+
+
 def parse_records(text):
-    rows = []
-    for line in text.splitlines():
-        if not line.strip():
-            continue
-        rows.append(line.split(","))
-    return rows
+    return [row for row in csv.reader(StringIO(text)) if any(field.strip() for field in row)]

@@ -10,6 +10,15 @@ class CsvRecordTest(unittest.TestCase):
     def test_quoted_comma(self):
         self.assertEqual(parse_records('name,note\nAda,"ships, fast"'), [["name", "note"], ["Ada", "ships, fast"]])
 
+    def test_escaped_double_quote(self):
+        self.assertEqual(parse_records('name,note\nAda,"says ""hi"""'), [["name", "note"], ["Ada", 'says "hi"']])
+
+    def test_blank_lines_are_skipped(self):
+        self.assertEqual(parse_records("\nname,note\n\nAda,ok\n   \n"), [["name", "note"], ["Ada", "ok"]])
+
+    def test_quoted_newline(self):
+        self.assertEqual(parse_records('name,note\nAda,"line one\nline two"'), [["name", "note"], ["Ada", "line one\nline two"]])
